newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian share prices slip in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian share prices slip in quiet trading.

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell on Sunday for the first time in four days in quiet trading which focused on the ever-popular banking and cement sectors.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all share index closed 1.89 points lower at 349.86 points. Turnover was an average 50.4 million pounds ($14.8 million), and only three stocks made up about a third of that total.

Last week, the market seemed to be perking up after falling to five-month lows in June. But despite Sunday's slippage, Rania Afifi of Intercaptial brokerage said the market was stable and prices were not following a downtrend.

"Prices are stabilising because there is buying support," said added. "Basically we do not see price jumps now. People are Commercial International Bank/CIB, the most active share, ended 1.44 pounds up at 72.45, when equity worth 5.68 million pounds was traded.
But another blue-chip bank, Egyptian American Bank shed 6.25 pounds to end at 123.75. "EAB went down despite the 1996 very good figures," said Afifi. "It's a very good bank."
The EAB said last month it would pay out a dividend of six pounds per share for calendar 1996. The bank said it would also increase its legal reserves by 60 million pounds to 120 million.
Fertiliser firm Egyptian Financial and Industrial, another busy share, ended down 0.50 at 202 pounds after 4.16 million pounds worth of shares changed hands.

Cement shares were also no exception the market's weaker prices. The sector's most active stock, Egyptian Tora Portland Cement, lost 1.48 pounds to close at 85.52. Shares worth 4.0 million pounds were traded.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 473.52 points from 473.45 while that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 260.27 from 262.38.
Of the 91 shares traded, 29 rose, 39 fell while 23 ended unchanged, the CMA said.
